messages.text:
Hi Hal,
Thanks for the detailed answers. That’s very helpful.
I’ve been rethinking which miner fits my setup best. It will run entirely on a separate solar system: five 410 W panels and a 5 kWh battery, with most of that going to the miner. I want the most hash per kWh, and I’d like it to run through the night on the battery without shutting off.
From the specs, the Harlo B30 in ECO mode (18 TH/s at 230 W, 12.8 J/TH) looks like a better fit than the 40T in Eco (30 TH/s at 450 W). The B30 should run 24 hours on my battery, and the 40T couldn’t make it through the night. Would you agree the B30 is the better choice for a solar-limited setup like mine?
If so, a few questions on the B30:

  1.  Is Batch 5 still shipping November 30, and what would the total be to a Florida address, with shipping and tax?
  2.  What is the warranty? Your email said 3 months on the 40T, but the product pages say the manufacturer’s warranty is at least 1 year. Which is correct for the B30?
  3.  Is Turbo (30 TH/s) the normal rated setting, or does running it void the warranty? The page says both.
  4.  Does it stay in ECO mode after a power loss or restart, without me having to reset it?
  5.  Can the fans be replaced, the same as on the 40T?
  6.  Does the LABORWEEK10 code on your site apply to the B30?

Thanks again,
Bill
Searched the catalog · Harlo B30 miner
Handed to the team · Warranty terms are being reconciled and the B30 page contradicts what was quoted

Hi Bill,

Yes, for your setup I would agree, and the battery is what decides it. In ECO the B30 draws 230 W, so overnight at twelve hours it takes about 2.8 kWh out of your 5 kWh battery and leaves you real margin. The 40T in Eco at 450 W wants about 5.4 kWh for the same twelve hours, which is your whole battery with nothing spare. On efficiency the B30 in ECO is 12.8 J/TH against the 40T's 15 J/TH in Eco, so you also get more hash per kWh. Eighteen terahash running all night beats thirty terahash that cuts out at 2am.

On price. The B30 is $899. I ran a checkout to a Florida address and sales tax came to $58.44, around 6.5 percent, and it moves a little by county. Shipping is calculated at checkout from your address and was $40 on the 40T run, so you are looking at roughly $1,000 delivered. The exact figures show before you pay. The L.10 code will not help, it expired on September 9, so please do not count on it.

On the ship date, the warranty and the Turbo question, I am not going to guess at any of them, because you have spotted a real contradiction and you deserve the answer in writing rather than my best reading of a page. Our listing shows the B30's three modes as Turbo 30 TH/s at 485 W, Balanced 24 TH/s at 350 W and ECO 18 TH/s at 230 W, which reads as three factory presets rather than an overclock, but whether Turbo sits inside the warranty is exactly the sort of thing I will not state from a product page. The warranty term, the Turbo position and the confirmed batch date for the B30 are with the team now, and a colleague is picking them up today, so you will have all three in this thread. The fan size and whether you can swap it yourself is in the same request.

Two I can answer. The mode you set is saved in the firmware, so after a power cut or a restart the unit comes back up in ECO without you touching anything, which matters on a solar system that cycles. And the B30 is a fan and heatsink design like the 40T, so a fan is a serviceable part, with the same caveat that opening the case is where warranty coverage stops. I would rather the team confirm the exact fan size with you than have me name one.

Nothing moves on the B30 price or stock in the meantime, and it is listed and buyable today.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Thank You Sarah trying not to be a PIA.
I really appreciate the feedback. Due to the current situation,  (NEW) there is limited information!  I need all the help I can get! 🙂

   Tks.
       Bill

Hi Bill,

You are not a PIA, and asking hard questions about a new machine is the right instinct, not a nuisance. I would rather you ask ten than buy on a guess.

So you have it in one place while you wait. The Harlo B30 is $899, Florida sales tax ran $58.44 on my test checkout at around 6.5 percent and it moves a little by county, and shipping shows at checkout from your address, which was $40 on the 40T run. Call it about $1,000 delivered. LABORWEEK10 has expired, so do not plan around it. For your five panels and a 5 kWh battery, the B30 in ECO at 230 W is the one I would put on that system, and it holds ECO through a power cut and restart without you resetting anything.

Still coming to you from the team today, and they are on now: the B30 warranty term, whether its 30 TH/s Turbo sits inside that warranty or outside it, the confirmed batch ship date, and the fan size with whether you can change it yourself. A colleague is picking those up and they land in this thread.

Nothing changes on the B30 price or availability while you decide, so take the time you need.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Hi JD,
Thanks for the quick answers, especially on the mode memory, the default setting and the fan videos. That helps a lot.
A few items from my earlier email are still open before I place the order for the B30:

  1.  Warranty: Which warranty applies to the B30, the 3-month RMA or the manufacturer’s 1-year warranty shown on the product page?
  2.  Price and shipping: What’s the total to a Florida address with shipping and tax, and is Batch 5 still shipping November 30?
  3.  Discount: Does the LABORWEEK10 code on your site apply to the B30?

Thanks again,
Bill

Hi Bill,

Two of the three I can settle right now, and I will be straight about the third.

Price to Florida on the B30: the unit is $899. I ran a checkout to a Florida address and sales tax came to $58.44, around 6.5 percent, which moves a little by county. Shipping is calculated at checkout from your address and came to $40 on the 40T run, so you are at roughly $997 all in. The exact figures show on the checkout page before you pay, and there are no duties or import fees on a US order.

Discount: LABORWEEK10 will not work on the B30. That code expired on September 9, so please do not build it into your numbers. If something new goes live it applies at checkout on the day.

Warranty and the Batch 5 date I am not going to answer from memory, because you have already caught our own pages disagreeing with each other and you would be right not to trust a third version from me. Which term covers the B30, the 3 month RMA or the 1 year manufacturer warranty, and the confirmed batch ship date, are both with the team. They are offline for the weekend and back Monday at 10am Eastern, and the answer comes to you here in this thread, so you do not need to chase it.

Nothing changes on the B30 price or availability over the weekend, so you lose nothing by deciding Monday with all three in hand.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Hi Sarah,
Before I place an order for the Harlo B30 (Batch 5), I need a few things answered in writing:

  1.
Out-the-door price: From your previous email I am assuming VERY close to $1000.00?
  2.  When I’m charged: Is my credit card charged when I order, or when the unit ships?
  3.  Where it ships from: Where is your warehouse? Does the unit ship from you, or directly from the manufacturer?
  4.  If the date slips: If Batch 5 doesn’t ship by November 30, will you notify me, and can I cancel for a full refund at that point?

I’ve read a great number of reviews describing long shipping delays and little communication. You’ve been very responsive with me, and I appreciate it, but I’d like to know what to expect before I commit.

P.S.
I really feel sorry for you and especially Abel. As a retired business for over 20 years, there is NO real excuse for all of this!
Thank you,
Bill D.

Hi Bill,

Taking them in order, and I will be plain where the answer is not what you would like.

Out the door, yes, very close to $1,000. The B30 is $899, Florida sales tax ran $58.44 on my test checkout at about 6.5 percent, and shipping was $40 on the run I did, so roughly $997. The exact numbers for your address appear on the checkout page before you confirm.

On the charge, your card is charged when you place the order, not when the unit ships. That is how a batch works at our end. What you pay goes into the build of a unit allocated to you, which is also why a pre-order is not a deposit you can walk back from casually. I would rather you know that before you click than after.

On where it ships from, a Florida address ships from our US fulfilment warehouse. It is our stock on our shelf, not a drop shipment from the manufacturer, so the box comes from us and a warranty return comes back to us rather than going overseas.

On the date slipping, here is the honest version. If a batch date moves, we email the address on the order, and you can watch the shipment itself on its way to us at https://heliumdeploy.com/pages/shipment-status, which shows each batch and which orders it covers. What I will not do is promise you in advance that a missed date equals a refund on request, because that is not mine to give and you would be right to hold me to it later. Cancellation requests go to a supervisor for review, and the usual first options are keeping the order, moving to an in stock unit, or store credit. If the date is the thing that decides this for you, I would rather you knew that now.

The reviews you have read about delays and silence are not imaginary, and I am not going to defend that. What I can control is this thread, and you have had an answer every time you wrote. The warranty question, which term covers the B30, and the confirmed Batch 5 date are still with the team. They are offline now and back tomorrow at 10am Eastern, and both answers come to you here.

And thank you for the postscript, that was kind of you.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy
